title: Six smaller things the build bot was asked for, each built within six minutes
summary: Six requests to @buildthis.bisks.net and what came back, by the posts' minute stamps. (1) Fri 13 Nov 04:43Z, @cee.wtf: "Pikmin clone where all your pikmin are Bluesky moots". 04:49Z: "pikmoot: your moots are the pikmin. pluck sprouts, hurl them at reply guys, haul treasure to the onion before dusk. same map per handle." (2) Fri 05:53Z, @vibecode.rodeo: take one of the bot's games "that features QWOP like controls" and "give it extremely straightforward and easy controls". 05:57Z: "Forked kinesin into kinesin-easy: hold → and the motor protein auto-walks hand-over-hand; release to refuel ATP." Told it was not loading, the bot checked and suggested a hard refresh. (3) Sun 15 Nov 02:33Z, @psingletary.com: "a page that scans all the moots and their posts for any music links and then returns all those links as a playlist". 02:36Z: mootmix. (4) Mon 16 Nov 00:27Z, @cee.wtf: "every post I've made that starts with “wow” or “#testimonials”". 00:29Z: wow-reel; a member replied "Wow". (5) Tue 17 Nov 02:18Z, @jessehattabaugh.com: a site that shows "recent posts/replies from your followers that haven't gotten any likes, quotes, or reposts so you can like, quote, and repost them", smaller accounts first. 02:22Z: unloved.bisks.net. (6) Tue 17 Nov 23:29Z, @harsimony.bsky.social mused that it is "Interesting to imagine a social media site where you can scroll through different software"; a member replied "Imagine? Where do you think you are right now"; on Wed 18 Nov at 04:33Z @shimmermathlabs.com asked the bot for it, filtering out "any junk like personal thoughts, politics, ai commentary or debate. we just want the sweet sweet software." 04:37Z: softscroll.

made.what: pikmoot: a Pikmin-like game where the creatures are your mutuals
kinesin-easy: an easy-controls version of the bot's game about a walking motor protein
mootmix: a playlist of the music links your mutuals have posted
wow-reel: every post by a handle that starts with "wow" or "#testimonials"
unloved: your followers' posts that nobody has liked, reposted or quoted, with one-tap like, repost and quote
softscroll: a day-by-day scroll of the software your mutuals posted

couldBeShown: Six one-line descriptions of six small sites, each beside the request that produced it. Research has seen none of the sites; everything known about them is in the bot's replies. kinesin-easy has the plainest picture: hold the right arrow and a motor protein "auto-walks hand-over-hand"; release "to refuel ATP"; "run out and you detach".
numbers: Request-to-build gaps by minute stamp: 6, 4, 3, 2, 4 and 4 minutes.
Five different requesters; two of them are not cluster members.
21 likes on the pikmoot request; the builds themselves have between 0 and 6 likes.

sensitive: @buildthis.bisks.net is a bot (R13): its posts are the persona of its operator, @bisks.net, and the account is marked featuredPrevious: shown. @psingletary.com (2,467 followers) and @jessehattabaugh.com (650) are not cluster members; each is here for a request the bot fulfilled. @brendigler.bsky.social (94 followers) is a small account whose one-word reply echoes the site's name. "unloved" lists real people's posts that got no response: its purpose is to give them some, and whose posts appear there is not in the data (R7 and R12 would apply to naming anyone). pikmoot's "hurl them at reply guys" is the bot's phrase for the game's opponents, a type and not a person. The softscroll request calls "personal thoughts, politics, ai commentary or debate" junk: the requester's joke about what to filter, not a view to restate. pikmoot and polykatamari borrow from commercial games. @shimmermathlabs.com is marked featuredPrevious: shown. @cee.wtf also appears in made-polykatamari and made-yard-shift-wheelie. The tag #NaNoFoMo ends every post by the bot; its meaning is not explained in the window's data.
notUnderstood: "kinesin": an earlier game of the bot's, named after a motor protein; research has not seen it.
"#testimonials" in the wow-reel request: a tag the requester uses; research does not know how.
